userStories.title: Stash restore in the .nax guard
acceptanceCriteria: With a `.nax` directory in the fixture root and `_naxStateGuardDeps.git` stubbed to return `"src/a.ts\0"` for `stash show`, `naxStateRefusalInText("git stash pop", ctx)` returns `undefined`.
With the same stub, `naxStateRefusalInText("git stash apply", ctx)` returns `undefined`.
With the same stub, `naxStateRefusalInText("git stash pop", ctx)` calls the stub with args `["stash", "show", "-z", "--name-only", "--no-renames", "--include-untracked", "stash@{0}"]`.
With the same stub, `naxStateRefusalInText("git stash pop --index 'stash@{1}'", ctx)` returns `undefined`.
With the same stub, `naxStateRefusalInText("git stash pop --index 'stash@{1}'", ctx)` calls the stub with ref `stash@{1}`.
With the same stub, `naxStateRefusalInText("git stash apply 2", ctx)` calls the stub with ref `2`.
`naxStateRefusalInText("git stash pop stash@{1}", ctx)` (unquoted ref) returns a defined refusal.
With the stub returning `"src/a.ts\0.nax/features/f/prd.json\0"`, `naxStateRefusalInText("git stash pop", ctx)` returns a defined refusal.
With the stub returning `"pkg/.nax/status.json\0"`, `naxStateRefusalInText("git stash apply", ctx)` returns a defined refusal.
With the stub returning `undefined`, `naxStateRefusalInText("git stash pop", ctx)` returns a defined refusal.
With two frames where the stub returns `"src/a.ts\0"` for the first and `undefined` for the second, `naxStateRefusal` for `git stash pop` returns a defined refusal.
`naxStateRefusalInText("git stash pop --hard-flag", ctx)` returns a defined refusal and does not call the stub.
`naxStateRefusalInText("git stash pop 'stash@{0}' extra", ctx)` returns a defined refusal.
`naxStateRefusalInText("git --future-flag x stash pop", ctx)` returns a defined refusal.
With the stub returning `"src/a.ts\0"` for `ls-files`, `naxStateRefusalInText("git stash push -- src", ctx)` returns `undefined`.
With the stub returning `"src/deep/a/b/c/.nax/prd.json\0"` for `ls-files`, `naxStateRefusalInText("git stash push -- src", ctx)` returns a defined refusal.
`naxStateRefusalInText("git stash push -- .", ctx)` returns a defined refusal.
`STASH_REFUSAL` does not include "named regular files".
`STASH_REFUSAL` includes "`pop` or `apply` of a stash that holds no `.nax` path".

In a real git repository with a committed `.nax/` directory, after `git stash push -- a.ts` of a modified `a.ts`, `naxStateRefusalInText("git stash pop", ctx)` with the default `_naxStateGuardDeps.git` returns `undefined`.
In the same kind of repository, after stashing a modification to `.nax/features/f/é.json`, `naxStateRefusalInText("git stash pop", ctx)` returns a defined refusal.
In the same kind of repository, after `git mv .nax/features/f/prd.json moved.json` and `git stash push`, `naxStateRefusalInText("git stash pop", ctx)` returns a defined refusal.

routing.reasoning: New module with shell-grammar parsing, multi-frame git listing and a guard that must fail closed; integration tests against real git. Not authentication, so lite TDD.

suggestedCriteria: `naxStateRefusalInText("git stash branch b", ctx)` still returns a defined refusal.
`naxStateRefusalInText("git stash save x", ctx)` still returns a defined refusal.
outOfScope: Allowing `pop`/`apply` of a stash that touches `.nax`, `git stash branch`, `stash save`, or an unquoted `stash@{N}` ref; they stay refused.
Rewording the guard's backstop refusal: a stash command whose git invocation the guard cannot classify (`time git stash pop`) is still refused with `STASH_REFUSAL`.

modifiedFiles.reason: the `stash` "denies %s when a .nax exists" table lists `"git stash push -- src"`, and `src` is a fixture directory with no `.nax` inside it, which US-001 allows. US-001 owns removing that one row (the allowance is pinned by US-001's own ACs) and stubbing `_naxStateGuardDeps.git` to return `undefined` in that file's `beforeEach`, restoring it in `afterEach`, so the `pop`, `apply` and `-c core.pager=x stash pop` rows stay refused without spawning git; every other row keeps its assertion that the refusal mentions `git diff HEAD` and `git show HEAD:`.

userStories.title: Loopback opt-in for the sandbox
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add `execution.sandbox.network.allowLocalBinding` and carry it through `buildSandboxPolicy` and srt's `SandboxManager.initialize` network so sandboxed commands can reach loopback ports (#2538).

**Motivation** — On macOS with a restricted network (`execution.sandbox.network.allowedDomains` set), srt confines sandboxed commands to its proxy ports, so a DB-backed test run in Bash gets `connection refused` from a test database that is up. srt's `allowLocalBinding` fixes it; nax has no way to set it.

**Approach** — `execution.sandbox.network.allowLocalBinding` (optional boolean; absent means off). It only changes anything with an `allowedDomains` list: with an open network srt's macOS profile already allows all network traffic, loopback included. srt reads `allowLocalBinding` only from the process-wide `SandboxManager.initialize` config (sandbox-runtime 0.0.77 `sandbox-manager.js` `getAllowLocalBinding`), never from a per-command `customConfig`. So `createSrtBackend(network)` passes it to `initialize` through `srtNetwork(allowedDomains, allowLocalBinding)`, and `customConfig` is unchanged. `srtNetwork(undefined, true)` returns the open-network object plus `allowLocalBinding: true`. `buildSandboxPolicy` sets `network.allowLocalBinding: true` on the policy when the config is `true`, for the ACP Claude sandbox, whose `claudeSandboxOptions` sends `network.allowLocalBinding: true` (with `allowedDomains` when the policy has them).

**Scope** — In: `SandboxConfigSchema.network` (schema: optional boolean), `SandboxNetworkPolicy` (policy: `allowLocalBinding?: true`), `buildSandboxPolicy`, `srtNetwork(allowedDomains, allowLocalBinding)`, `createSrtBackend`. Out: `claudeSandboxOptions` (US-004); per-port grants; per-package `allowLocalBinding` (srt reads it once per process); Linux behaviour; bumping sandbox-runtime.

**Interface**
```ts
// SandboxConfigSchema.network: allowLocalBinding optional boolean
// SandboxNetworkPolicy: allowLocalBinding?: true
srtNetwork(allowedDomains, allowLocalBinding)
```
acceptanceCriteria: `SandboxConfigSchema.parse({})` yields a `network` with no `allowLocalBinding` value.
`SandboxConfigSchema.parse({ network: { allowLocalBinding: true } })` yields `network.allowLocalBinding === true`.

`buildSandboxPolicy` with `network: { allowedDomains: ["registry.npmjs.org"], allowLocalBinding: true }` returns a policy whose `network` equals `{ allowedDomains: ["registry.npmjs.org"], allowLocalBinding: true }`.
`buildSandboxPolicy` with `network: { allowLocalBinding: true }` returns a policy whose `network` equals `{ allowLocalBinding: true }`.
`buildSandboxPolicy` with the default network returns a policy whose `network` has no `allowLocalBinding` key.

An srt backend from `createSrtBackend({ allowedDomains: ["x.test"], allowLocalBinding: true })`, with `_srtBackendDeps.load` stubbed, passes `network.allowLocalBinding: true` to `SandboxManager.initialize` on its first `wrap`.
An srt backend from `createSrtBackend({ allowLocalBinding: true })` passes an `initialize` network with no `allowedDomains` key and `allowLocalBinding: true`.
An srt backend from `createSrtBackend({ allowedDomains: ["x.test"] })` passes an `initialize` network with no `allowLocalBinding` key.
The `customConfig` passed to `wrapWithSandboxArgv` for a policy with `allowLocalBinding: true` has no `allowLocalBinding` key.

routing.reasoning: Optional config flag threaded through schema, policy builder and srt initialize; four files, standard patterns.

outOfScope: A per-port loopback grant; srt grants every loopback port when `allowLocalBinding` is on.
A per-package `allowLocalBinding`: srt reads it once per process, so the first backend's value applies to the whole run.
Linux behaviour of `allowLocalBinding` (bwrap uses its own network namespace); the flag is passed through unverified there.
Bumping `@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime` past 0.0.77.

outOfScope: MCP instructions on nax-agent's own `createAgentSession` path (the nax-agent ACP server); only nax's sessions get them.
Pinning MCP server instructions in `.nax/mcp-lock.json`; the text is sanitised for control characters and capped, not locked.
Filtering MCP instructions per tool after deny or ask rules; a provider with at least one advertised tool gets its instructions delivered.

userStories.title: ACP bridge instructions and Claude loopback
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Deliver MCP instructions to the ACP agent through the tool host's `initialize` result, and send `network.allowLocalBinding` in the Claude sandbox options.

**Motivation** — ACP Claude sessions must receive the same server instructions as native sessions (#2517), and macOS sandboxed ACP Claude commands need loopback access when the project opts in (#2538).

**Approach** — ACP: nax's `openContext` sets `BackendOpenContext.providerInstructions` from `opts.providerInstructions` only when `finalizeAcpSurface` delivered at least one tool (that part is US-005). The nax-agent-acp backend's `toolHostFor` passes `ctx.providerInstructions` to `createToolHost(calls, token, { instructions })`, and `serveMcp` constructs its `Server` with `instructions` when set, so the ACP agent's MCP client receives it in `initialize`. Loopback: `buildSandboxPolicy` (US-002) sets `network.allowLocalBinding: true` on the policy when the config is `true`, for the ACP Claude sandbox, whose `claudeSandboxOptions` sends `network.allowLocalBinding: true` (with `allowedDomains` when the policy has them).

**Scope** — In: `createToolHost(calls, token, opts?: { instructions?: string })` and `serveMcp` in packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/tool-host.ts, `toolHostFor` in client/backend.ts, `claudeSandboxOptions(policy)` in client/claude-sandbox.ts. Out: nax-side `openContext` population (US-005); nax-agent policy/schema (US-002) and `BackendOpenContext.providerInstructions` declaration (US-003); verifying against the Claude Agent SDK that `SandboxSettings.network.allowLocalBinding` is honoured.

**Interface**
```ts
createToolHost(calls, token, opts?: { instructions?: string })
```
acceptanceCriteria: A tool host from `createToolHost(calls, token, { instructions: "Pass the repo root as project" })`, started and sent an MCP `initialize` request with its token, answers with `result.instructions` equal to that text.
A tool host from `createToolHost(calls, token)` answers `initialize` with no `instructions` field.
`toolHostFor` for a `BackendOpenContext` with `providerInstructions: "X"` and a token creates the tool host with `instructions: "X"` (stubbed `createToolHost` captures the options).
`toolHostFor` for a context with no `providerInstructions` creates the tool host with no `instructions` option.
`claudeSandboxOptions` for a policy whose `network` is `{ allowedDomains: ["x.test"], allowLocalBinding: true }` returns `network` equal to `{ allowedDomains: ["x.test"], allowLocalBinding: true }`.
`claudeSandboxOptions` for a policy whose `network` is `{ allowLocalBinding: true }` returns `network` equal to `{ allowLocalBinding: true }`.
`claudeSandboxOptions` for a policy whose `network` is `{}` returns no `network` key.
`claudeSandboxOptions` for a policy from nax-agent's `buildSandboxPolicy` with `network.allowLocalBinding: true` returns `network.allowLocalBinding === true`.

routing.reasoning: Three files in one package, additive optional parameters, standard patterns.

outOfScope: Verifying against the Claude Agent SDK that `SandboxSettings.network.allowLocalBinding` is honoured; this story pins only the options nax sends.

userStories.title: Commit prd.json after each status write
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Commit `prd.json` after every story status write via a new `commitPrdProgress` / `savePrdProgress`, wired into the completion stage, result handler and queue-check stage (#2533).

**Motivation** — The completion stage writes `prd.json` but never commits it. The next story's agent sees a modified file it did not touch, the next `autoCommitIfDirty` sweeps the status change into the wrong story's commit, and a stray `git checkout .` resets finished stories to `pending` (#2490).

**Approach** — PRD commit (#2533).
- `commitPrdProgress({ prdPath, feature, storyId, label })` (new, `src/prd/progress-commit.ts`, exported from `@/prd`) runs git through `_prdCommitDeps.git` (`gitWithTimeout`) with `cwd = dirname(prdPath)` and pathspec `basename(prdPath)`: `git add -- <prd>`; when `git diff --cached --quiet -- <prd>` exits 0 it returns `false`; else `git commit --no-verify -m "chore(<feature>): progress <storyId> <label>" -- <prd>`. No `[skip ci]`, for the reason `commitLedger` gives. A failed `add` because the PRD is ignored returns `false` silently (checked first with `git check-ignore -q -- <prd>`, exit 0 = ignored); any other git failure logs one `warn` with the story id and returns `false`. It never throws.
- `savePrdProgress(prd, prdPath, storyId, label)` (new, `src/prd/progress-commit.ts`) calls `savePRD` and then `commitPrdProgress` with `feature: prd.feature`; call sites replace their `savePRD` line with it, one line for one line, because `execution/pipeline-result-handler.ts` is 598 of the 600-line source limit and must not grow.
- Call sites and labels: the completion stage keeps its `_completionDeps.savePRD` call and, right after it and only when `persistPrd`, calls a new `_completionDeps.commitPrdProgress` (`passed`); `handlePipelineFailure` `pause` (`paused`) and `fail` (`failed`); `failStoryAfterMerge` (`failed`); `queueCheckStage` ABORT (`aborted`, story id `_run`), RETRY (`retry`), PRIORITY (`priority`), INJECT (`inject`) and SKIP (`skipped`), through a new `_queueCheckDeps.savePrdProgress`. `pipeline-result-handler.ts` reaches it through a new `_resultHandlerDeps.savePrdProgress`.

**Scope** — In: new src/prd/progress-commit.ts (`commitPrdProgress`, `savePrdProgress`, `_prdCommitDeps`) exported from `@/prd`; `_completionDeps` (pipeline/stages/completion.ts); `_resultHandlerDeps` (execution/pipeline-result-handler.ts); new exported `_queueCheckDeps = { savePrdProgress }` in pipeline/stages/queue-check.ts. Out: ledger commits (US-007); the parallel worktree executor (its unified executor stays the single writer); a dry-run-specific branch in `commitPrdProgress`.

**Interface**
```ts
commitPrdProgress({ prdPath, feature, storyId, label })  // resolves true when a commit was created, false otherwise; never throws
savePrdProgress(prd, prdPath, storyId, label)
_prdCommitDeps.git  // gitWithTimeout
_completionDeps.commitPrdProgress
_resultHandlerDeps.savePrdProgress
_queueCheckDeps = { savePrdProgress }
```

**Failure handling** — A `commitPrdProgress` git step fails: one `warn` with the story id; returns `false`; the story outcome is unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: In a real git repository with a tracked `prd.json`, `commitPrdProgress` after a status change creates a commit whose message is `chore(f): progress US-001 passed`.
The same commit contains only the PRD.
The same call returns `true`.
An unrelated staged edit stays staged and is absent from that commit.
An unrelated unstaged edit stays unstaged and is absent from that commit.
`commitPrdProgress` on an unchanged PRD returns `false` and creates no commit.
`commitPrdProgress` on a PRD ignored by `.gitignore` returns `false` and logs no `warn`.
`commitPrdProgress` passes `--no-verify` to `git commit` and no message containing `[skip ci]`.
`commitPrdProgress` with `_prdCommitDeps.git` failing the commit step logs one `warn` with the story id and returns `false` without throwing.
`savePrdProgress` calls `savePRD` before `commitPrdProgress`.
`completionStage.execute` with `persistPrd` true calls `_completionDeps.commitPrdProgress` once, after `_completionDeps.savePRD`, with the story id and label `passed`.
`completionStage.execute` with `ctx.skipPrdPersistence` true calls neither `_completionDeps.savePRD` nor `_completionDeps.commitPrdProgress`.
`handlePipelineFailure` for a `fail` result calls `_resultHandlerDeps.savePrdProgress` with label `failed`.
`handlePipelineFailure` for a `pause` result calls `_resultHandlerDeps.savePrdProgress` with label `paused`.

`handlePipelineSuccess` with `storyIsolation: "worktree"` and `_resultHandlerDeps.mergeEngine.merge` stubbed to return `{ success: false, failureKind: "error" }` calls `_resultHandlerDeps.savePrdProgress` with label `failed`.
`queueCheckStage.execute` handling a `SKIP` command for a story in the PRD calls `_queueCheckDeps.savePrdProgress` with that story id and label `skipped`.
`queueCheckStage.execute` handling an `ABORT` command calls `_queueCheckDeps.savePrdProgress` with story id `_run` and label `aborted`.
`queueCheckStage.execute` handling a `RETRY` command calls `_queueCheckDeps.savePrdProgress` with label `retry`.

routing.reasoning: One new module plus one-line call-site swaps in three files; the 600-line cap on pipeline-result-handler.ts requires line-for-line replacement.

suggestedCriteria: `queueCheckStage.execute` handling a `PRIORITY` command calls `_queueCheckDeps.savePrdProgress` with label `priority`.
`queueCheckStage.execute` handling an `INJECT` command calls `_queueCheckDeps.savePrdProgress` with label `inject`.
outOfScope: A dry-run-specific branch in `commitPrdProgress`.
Committing `prd.json` from the parallel worktree executor; its unified executor stays the single writer.

userStories.title: Commit the ledger and report hidden nax files
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Commit the advisor ledger even when a broad `.gitignore` rule hides it (`add -f`), report ignored nax-tracked paths in precheck and `nax init`, and make a failed workflow ledger commit loud (#2534).

**Motivation** — `commitLedger` runs `git add -- <ledger>`. In repos whose `.gitignore` predates the ledger (`.nax/**/*.jsonl` in 6 of 9 local repos), the add fails, publishing continues, and the PR ships without the advisor rulings its body cites. The only signal is one warn line.

**Approach** — Ledger (#2534).
- `commitLedger` (workflow) runs `git add -f -- <exact ledger path>`; so does the ledger `add` in `finish/advise.ts`.
- `findIgnoredNaxTrackedPaths(projectDir)` (new, `src/utils/ignored-nax-paths.ts`) checks the ledger, `spec.md` and `prd.json` paths for a probe feature id, built with `ledgerPath` and `featureDir` from `@/config` / `@/advisor`, through `git check-ignore -v --no-index -- <paths>` (no `-z`: git refuses `-z` without `--stdin`) run by `gitWithTimeout` behind `_ignoredNaxPathsDeps.git`. Each output line is `<source>:<line>:<pattern><TAB><path>`; it returns `{ path, rule }` per line whose pattern does not start with `!` (a negation means the path is re-included), with `rule` = `<source>:<line>:<pattern>`. A non-zero exit other than 1 ("nothing ignored"), or a spawn failure, returns `[]`.
- `checkGitignoreCoversNax` (precheck) fails with a message naming each path, its rule, and the fix: add `!.nax/features/*/<file>`, or replace a wholesale `features/*/` rule, because a negation cannot re-include under an ignored directory. `nax init` logs the same text as one `warn` per path after patching `.gitignore`.
- `ledgerCommit` in `workflow/finalize.ts` returns a result `{ committed: boolean; missingRulings: number }`; `pushLedger` reads `.committed`. When `commitLedger` throws and the ledger has N > 0 non-empty lines, it logs one `warn` "Advisor ledger commit failed — the branch is missing N advisor rulings" and returns `missingRulings: N`. The first ledger commit of each publishing mode (`none`, local-only, `push`, `pr`) appends the readiness reason `advisor ledger not committed: the branch is missing N advisor rulings` to that mode's reasons, so the PR stays a draft and the advisor is not asked. `pushLedger`'s second commit only logs. `finish/advise.ts` ignores git exit codes today; only the workflow path gets the loud signal.

**Scope** — In: `commitLedger` (workflow/git.ts), `ledgerCommit` and `pushLedger` (workflow/finalize.ts), the ledger add in finish/advise.ts, new utils/ignored-nax-paths.ts (`findIgnoredNaxTrackedPaths`, `_ignoredNaxPathsDeps`), `checkGitignoreCoversNax` (precheck/checks-warnings.ts), `nax init` (cli/init.ts). Out: a loud failed-ledger signal in pipeline-mode finish; removing broad `.gitignore` rules automatically; PRD commits (US-006).

**Interface**
```ts
findIgnoredNaxTrackedPaths(projectDir: string): Promise<{ path: string; rule: string }[]>
ledgerCommit(fc): Promise<{ committed: boolean; missingRulings: number }>
_ignoredNaxPathsDeps.git
```

**Failure handling** — `commitLedger` throws in a workflow publishing mode: publishing continues; the warn and the readiness reason name the missing ruling count. `git check-ignore` fails (not a repo, git missing): `findIgnoredNaxTrackedPaths` returns `[]`; no warning.
acceptanceCriteria: `commitLedger` calls git with `["add", "-f", "--", <ledger path>]`.
In a real git repository whose `.gitignore` contains `.nax/**/*.jsonl`, `commitLedger` commits `.nax/features/f/decisions.jsonl` and returns `true`.
In the same repository an unrelated staged file stays staged and out of the ledger commit.
The ledger commit in `finish/advise.ts` calls git `add` with `-f` before `--`.
`findIgnoredNaxTrackedPaths` in a repository whose `.gitignore` has `**/.nax/features/*/` returns three entries, for the ledger, `spec.md` and `prd.json`.
Each of those entries has a `rule` naming `.gitignore` and `**/.nax/features/*/`.
`findIgnoredNaxTrackedPaths` in a repository whose `.gitignore` is exactly `NAX_GITIGNORE_ENTRIES` returns `[]`.
`findIgnoredNaxTrackedPaths` in a repository whose `.gitignore` has `.nax/**/*.jsonl` and `!.nax/features/*/decisions.jsonl` returns `[]`.
`findIgnoredNaxTrackedPaths` returns `[]` when `_ignoredNaxPathsDeps.git` exits 128.
`checkGitignoreCoversNax` with one ignored ledger entry reported returns a failing check whose message names the rule.
The same check's message includes `!.nax/features/*/decisions.jsonl`.
`nax init` on a project where `findIgnoredNaxTrackedPaths` reports one entry logs one `warn` naming the path and rule.
`publish` in `none` mode with `_featureDeps.commitLedger` throwing and a 3-line ledger logs a `warn` containing "the branch is missing 3 advisor rulings".
The same `publish` returns reasons including `advisor ledger not committed: the branch is missing 3 advisor rulings`.
`publish` in `pr` mode with `commitLedger` throwing and a 3-line ledger opens the PR as a draft and never calls the advisor's approval.
`publish` in `push` mode with `commitLedger` throwing and a 3-line ledger returns reasons including the ledger reason.
`publish` with no forge target, `commitLedger` throwing and a 3-line ledger returns reasons including the ledger reason.
`publish` with `commitLedger` throwing and an empty ledger adds no ledger reason.

routing.reasoning: Five existing files plus one new util; standard git/precheck patterns with a return-type change in ledgerCommit/pushLedger.

suggestedCriteria: `commitLedger` in a repository whose `.gitignore` does not ignore the ledger still commits it and returns `true`.
outOfScope: Removing broad `.gitignore` rules automatically; precheck and `nax init` only report them.
A loud failed-ledger signal in pipeline-mode finish (`finish/advise.ts`), which ignores git exit codes today.

userStories.title: Host-side e2e gate
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add `quality.commands.e2e` and optional `e2eSetup` as a host-run repository gate, and expose `e2e` (but not `e2eSetup`) to agents through `RunCommand` with the full-suite timeout (#2530).

**Motivation** — Chromium cannot launch inside srt on macOS: its `bootstrap_check_in` Mach service registration is denied. srt 0.0.79 (latest, 2026-10-07) still allows only `mach-lookup` rules, so no setting enables it. E2e journeys therefore ship unexecuted. The fix runs them on the host.

**Approach** — E2e gate (#2530).
- `quality.commands.e2e` and `quality.commands.e2eSetup` (both `QualityCommandSpecSchema`, optional, layerable per package like the other keys).
- `GATE_ORDER` becomes `build, typecheck, lint, test, e2e`. `GateCommand` gains an optional `setup`; `resolveGateCommands` attaches the same layer's `e2eSetup` to that layer's `e2e` gate and includes `setup` in its dedupe key. `e2eSetup` without `e2e` produces no gate.
- `runQualityGates` runs a gate's `setup` first, through `_qualityGateDeps.run` with the gate's `cwd`, the same timeout and `commandName` `<name>:setup`. A non-zero setup exit marks the gate failing without running its command; the chunk is `[<name>] exit=<setup exit>` then `setup failed:` and the setup output.
- Workflow repo gates (`runRepoGates`, used for repo-gates and final gates) and pipeline finish (`finish/gates-loop.ts`) reach e2e through these two functions, on the host.
- Agents: `extractDispatchConfigFields` drops `e2eSetup` from `commands`, so `RunCommand` never offers it; `e2e` stays declared and joins `SUITE_COMMAND_NAMES` for the full-suite timeout.

**Scope** — In: `QualityConfigSchema.commands` (config/schemas-execution.ts) and the hand-written `QualityConfig.commands` (config/runtime-types.ts) adding `e2e?`, `e2eSetup?` to both; `GATE_ORDER`, `GateCommand`, `resolveGateCommands`, `runQualityGates` (finish/gates/quality.ts); `runRepoGates` (workflow/repo-gates.ts); `extractDispatchConfigFields`, `SUITE_COMMAND_NAMES` (agents/dispatch-config-fields.ts). No gate fixture configures `e2e`, so expected gate lists are unchanged. Out: prompt text about e2e (US-009); running e2e inside an agent's Bash sandbox; a blocking host-side pre-run setup step for the whole run (#2521); e2e result parsing into per-test findings.

**Interface**
```ts
// QualityConfigSchema.commands / QualityConfig.commands
e2e?: QualityCommandSpec; e2eSetup?: QualityCommandSpec;
// GATE_ORDER = build, typecheck, lint, test, e2e
// GateCommand gains an optional `setup` (the same layer's e2eSetup command); included in the resolveGateCommands dedupe key
```

**Failure handling** — `e2eSetup` exits non-zero: the `e2e` gate fails without running `e2e`.
acceptanceCriteria: `QualityConfigSchema.parse({ commands: { e2e: "bunx playwright test", e2eSetup: "docker compose up -d" } })` keeps both keys.
`resolveGateCommands` for root commands `test` and `e2e` returns gate names `["test", "e2e"]`.
`resolveGateCommands` for root `e2e` and `e2eSetup` returns an `e2e` gate whose `setup` is the `e2eSetup` command.
`resolveGateCommands` for root `e2eSetup` without `e2e` returns no gate named `e2e` or `e2eSetup`.
`resolveGateCommands` for a package overlay setting `e2e` and `e2eSetup` returns an `e2e@<pkg>` gate with that overlay's `setup` and the package `cwd`.
`resolveGateCommands` for a root and a package overlay with the same `e2e` command and cwd but different `e2eSetup` keeps both gates.
`runQualityGates` for an `e2e` gate with a `setup` calls `_qualityGateDeps.run` for `e2e:setup` before `e2e`.
Both of those calls use the gate's `cwd`.
`runQualityGates` for an `e2e` gate whose setup exits 1 does not run the `e2e` command.
The same run lists `e2e` in `failing` and its output chunk starts `[e2e] exit=1\nsetup failed:`.
`runQualityGates` for an `e2e` gate whose command exits 1 after a passing setup lists `e2e` in `failing`.
`runRepoGates` with stubbed `_qualityGateDeps` and a config declaring a failing `e2e` returns a finding whose issue starts `repo gate e2e failed:`.
`extractDispatchConfigFields` for commands `{ test, e2e, e2eSetup }` returns `commands` without `e2eSetup`.
The same call returns `commands` with `e2e`.
The declared-command runner bound with the dispatch fields applies the full-suite timeout to a request naming `e2e`.

routing.reasoning: Extends an existing gate table with one more key and an optional setup step across five known files using established patterns; no new abstraction, so single-session TDD suffices.

suggestedCriteria: `resolveGateCommands` for root commands `build`, `typecheck`, `lint` and `test` with no `e2e` returns the same gate names as before, with no `e2e` gate.
`runQualityGates` for a gate with no `setup` calls `_qualityGateDeps.run` once, for the gate command only.
outOfScope: Running e2e inside an agent's Bash sandbox, or an unsandboxed Bash allowlist for `playwright test`.
A blocking host-side pre-run setup step for the whole run (#2521); `e2eSetup` runs only before the `e2e` gate.
E2e result parsing into per-test findings; a red e2e gate carries the output tail like every repo gate.

userStories.title: Workflow prompts: failing-run rule and e2e awareness
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Change the workflow implementer and story review prompts to require the failing run before the implementation (accepting an honest not-captured note), and add e2e-gate awareness lines passed by the workflow callers (#2540, #2530).

**Motivation** — The implementer prompt demands a failing run per AC, and implementers that wrote test and code together fake it afterwards by stashing their own implementation; and Chromium cannot launch inside srt on macOS, so agents must run e2e via `RunCommand` on the host.

**Approach** — RED evidence (#2540). `buildWorkflowImplementPrompt`'s step 1 becomes: "TDD for every acceptance criterion: write the test, run it, and capture the failing run before you write the implementation for that criterion; then write the code and capture the passing run. Never stash, revert, move or copy aside implementation files to produce a failing run afterwards." Its **TDD evidence** report bullet is rewritten to: "for each AC, the failing run and the passing run (command and the relevant output lines). If you did not capture the failing run, say so under **Decisions & assumptions**; then evidence that the test exercises the new code path is acceptable. Missing evidence without that note, or a test that asserts nothing, fails review." `buildWorkflowStoryReviewPrompt`'s spec verdict sentence becomes "missing evidence for an AC (other than an honest not-captured note), or a test that asserts nothing, is a spec failure", followed by: "A report that says the failing run was not captured is not a spec failure when the test exercises the new code path. A failing run produced by reverting or stashing the implementation is a finding."

E2e prompts (#2530): `buildWorkflowImplementPrompt` and `buildWorkflowStoryReviewPrompt` accept `e2eGate?: boolean`. Implementer text when true: "Browser e2e tests cannot launch inside the Bash sandbox. Run the e2e suite only with `RunCommand {\"command\":\"e2e\"}`; nax also runs it as a repository gate once every story is done." Story review text when true: "nax runs the e2e suite as a repository gate on the host; do not list e2e journeys in cannotVerify." Callers pass `e2eGate: sc.config.quality?.commands?.e2e !== undefined`: `promptFor`'s `implement` arm and its fresh `restart` arm, and `runStoryReview`.

**Scope** — In: packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/workflow-implementer-builder.ts, workflow-story-review-builder.ts, `promptFor` in workflow/implement.ts (reached through the exported `runImplementerTurn`), `runStoryReview` in workflow/story-review.ts. Out: the `quality.commands.e2e` config key and gate (US-008); changing the workflow fix prompt's TDD wording - only the implement and fresh restart prompts change.

**Interface**
```ts
// buildWorkflowImplementPrompt and buildWorkflowStoryReviewPrompt each accept an optional input field:
e2eGate?: boolean
```
acceptanceCriteria: `buildWorkflowImplementPrompt` includes "capture the failing run before you write the implementation for that criterion".
The same prompt includes "Never stash, revert, move or copy aside implementation files to produce a failing run afterwards".
The same prompt includes "If you did not capture the failing run, say so under **Decisions & assumptions**".
The same prompt includes "evidence that the test exercises the new code path is acceptable".
`buildWorkflowStoryReviewPrompt` includes "A report that says the failing run was not captured is not a spec failure when the test exercises the new code path".
The same story review prompt includes "A failing run produced by reverting or stashing the implementation is a finding".
`buildWorkflowImplementPrompt` with `e2eGate: true` includes `RunCommand {"command":"e2e"}`.
The same prompt includes "Browser e2e tests cannot launch inside the Bash sandbox".
`buildWorkflowImplementPrompt` without `e2eGate` does not include `RunCommand {"command":"e2e"}`.
`buildWorkflowStoryReviewPrompt` with `e2eGate: true` includes "do not list e2e journeys in cannotVerify".
`buildWorkflowStoryReviewPrompt` without `e2eGate` does not include "e2e journeys".
`runImplementerTurn` for an `implement` turn, with `sc.config.quality.commands.e2e` set, sends a prompt (stubbed `_workflowDeps.callOp` captures it) including `RunCommand {"command":"e2e"}`.
`runImplementerTurn` for a fresh `restart` turn with the same config sends a prompt including `RunCommand {"command":"e2e"}`.
`runImplementerTurn` for an `implement` turn with no `e2e` command sends a prompt without `RunCommand {"command":"e2e"}`.
`runStoryReview` with `sc.config.quality.commands.e2e` set sends a prompt including "do not list e2e journeys in cannotVerify" (stubbed `callOp` captures it).

routing.reasoning: Prompt text edits in two builders plus two caller flags; exact-string assertions, standard patterns.

suggestedCriteria: The workflow fix prompt does not include "capture the failing run before you write the implementation for that criterion".
`runStoryReview` with no `e2e` command sends a prompt without "do not list e2e journeys in cannotVerify".
outOfScope: Changing the workflow fix prompt's TDD wording; only the implement and fresh restart prompts change.
Running e2e inside an agent's Bash sandbox, or an unsandboxed Bash allowlist for `playwright test`.

analysis:
Seven independent fixes (#2539 #2540 #2534 #2533 #2517 #2538 #2530) landing before stable 0.88.0, split into nine binding stories across packages/nax-agent (US-001..003), packages/nax-agent-acp (US-004) and packages/nax (US-005..009). Dependency direction is nax-ai -> nax-agent -> nax and nax-agent -> nax-agent-acp (peer); US-004 depends on US-002 (SandboxNetworkPolicy.allowLocalBinding) and US-003 (BackendOpenContext.providerInstructions); US-005 depends on US-003 (ToolProvider.instructions, ResolvedProviderTools.instructions, renderProviderInstructions, OpenSessionOpts.providerInstructions, buildCodingToolSupport); US-009 depends on US-008 (quality.commands.e2e config key).

Key files and constraints:
- US-001: packages/nax-agent/src/tools/nax-state-guard.ts is 514 of 600 lines, so new logic goes in the new packages/nax-agent/src/tools/nax-stash-restore.ts and stashRefusal stays a thin dispatch. nax-agent src/ has no spawnSync today; Bun.* is banned by check:no-bun-apis; every git argv must use gitSpawnEnv() (packages/nax-agent/src/internal/git-env.ts) for check-git-spawn-env; GIT_TIMEOUT_MS lives in src/internal/git-exec.ts. The existing test packages/nax-agent/test/unit/tools/nax-state-guard.test.ts has a 'git stash push -- src' deny row that US-001 must remove, and must stub _naxStateGuardDeps.git to undefined in beforeEach (restore in afterEach). The shell tokenizer in naxStateRefusalInText ends a segment at { and }, so an unquoted stash@{1} becomes ref 'stash@' and is refused; quoted form is allowed. Every working-directory frame (ctx.frames) must list cleanly. The directory-pathspec allow decision replaces the bounded scanNaxDirs walk (nax-dirs.ts).
- US-002: srt reads allowLocalBinding only from process-wide SandboxManager.initialize config (sandbox-runtime 0.0.77), never from customConfig, so createSrtBackend(network) must pass it via srtNetwork(allowedDomains, allowLocalBinding) to initialize while customConfig stays unchanged. buildSandboxPolicy sets network.allowLocalBinding: true only when config is true (no key otherwise). Files: config/schemas-sandbox.ts, sandbox/policy-builder.ts, sandbox/srt-backend.ts, sandbox/types.ts.
- US-003: connectMcp (mcp/connect.ts) reads client.getInstructions() after tool listing; set only for non-empty string. ToolProvider (tools/provider-types.ts) gains optional instructions(workdir); resolveProviderTools (tools/provider-advertise.ts) calls it only for attached providers with >=1 tool after admits. New tools/provider-instructions.ts with renderProviderInstructions and caps; export from package entry AND regenerate packages/nax-agent/api/nax-agent.api.txt via api:update (check:api). Native session folds providerInstructions into the existing systemPrompts entry via recordSystemPrompt (NO new state map; session-adapter.test.ts asserts every state collection holds the session). systemFieldFor returns { system }.
- US-004: createToolHost(calls, token, opts?) and serveMcp Server construction with instructions; toolHostFor passes ctx.providerInstructions; claudeSandboxOptions sends network.allowLocalBinding (with allowedDomains when present, no network key when policy network is empty).
- US-005: nax McpServerSchema (config/schemas-mcp.ts, .strict() kept) and hand-written McpServerConfig interface (config/runtime-types-mcp.ts) both need instructions. McpPool.instructions is optional on the type so hand-built fixtures still typecheck. The provider combines pool text + blank line + config text with {workdir} substituted; withheld-tool warn fires once per server id on the first tools(workdir) listing. resolveCodingToolSupport renders and logs one info on the mcp channel. OpenSessionRequest (session/types.ts), build-hop-callback-hop.ts, open-session-extras.ts and agents/acp/open-context.ts (only when finalizeAcpSurface delivered at least one tool) forward it.
- US-006: packages/nax/src/execution/pipeline-result-handler.ts is 598 of 600 lines and must NOT grow: replace savePRD lines one-for-one with savePrdProgress via a new _resultHandlerDeps.savePrdProgress. New src/prd/progress-commit.ts exported from @/prd. Completion stage keeps _completionDeps.savePRD and adds _completionDeps.commitPrdProgress only when persistPrd. queue-check.ts gets a new exported _queueCheckDeps = { savePrdProgress }. No [skip ci]; --no-verify; never throws.
- US-007: workflow/git.ts commitLedger -> add -f; finish/advise.ts ledger add -> add -f; new utils/ignored-nax-paths.ts (findIgnoredNaxTrackedPaths via git check-ignore -v --no-index, no -z); precheck/checks-warnings.ts checkGitignoreCoversNax and cli/init.ts report; workflow/finalize.ts ledgerCommit returns { committed, missingRulings } and pushLedger reads .committed; first ledger commit of each publishing mode (none, local-only, push, pr) appends the readiness reason; pushLedger second commit only logs. Pipeline-mode finish stays silent.
- US-008: finish/gates/quality.ts GATE_ORDER adds e2e, GateCommand.setup, dedupe key includes setup, setup runs first as <name>:setup; workflow/repo-gates.ts reaches e2e through resolveGateCommands/runQualityGates; agents/dispatch-config-fields.ts drops e2eSetup from commands and adds e2e to SUITE_COMMAND_NAMES; QualityConfigSchema.commands (config/schemas-execution.ts) and hand-written QualityConfig.commands (config/runtime-types.ts) both need e2e?/e2eSetup?.
- US-009: prompt builders workflow-implementer-builder.ts and workflow-story-review-builder.ts take e2eGate?: boolean; callers workflow/implement.ts promptFor (implement arm and fresh restart arm) and workflow/story-review.ts runStoryReview pass sc.config.quality?.commands?.e2e !== undefined. The workflow fix prompt's TDD wording must not change.

Risks: file-size caps (600 source lines) on nax-state-guard.ts and pipeline-result-handler.ts; dual type declarations (zod schema + hand-written interfaces) for mcp and quality config must be kept in sync; public API snapshot for nax-agent; barrel/circular import init-order (import new symbols from leaf modules); existing tests that assert state collections or gate lists must stay unchanged because all new fields are optional. Run package commands from the package directory; never bare bun test.
outOfScope: Bumping `@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime` past 0.0.77. srt 0.0.79 still has no Mach service registration rule, so a bump would not let Chromium launch inside the sandbox.
Running e2e inside an agent's Bash sandbox, or an unsandboxed Bash allowlist for `playwright test`.
A blocking host-side pre-run setup step for the whole run (#2521); `e2eSetup` runs only before the `e2e` gate.
A per-port loopback grant; srt grants every loopback port when `allowLocalBinding` is on.
A per-package `allowLocalBinding`: srt reads it once per process, so the first backend's value applies to the whole run.
Linux behaviour of `allowLocalBinding` (bwrap uses its own network namespace); the flag is passed through unverified there.
US-004 only: verifying against the Claude Agent SDK that `SandboxSettings.network.allowLocalBinding` is honoured; US-004 pins only the options nax sends.
US-001 only: allowing `pop`/`apply` of a stash that touches `.nax`, `git stash branch`, `stash save`, or an unquoted `stash@{N}` ref; they stay refused.
Pinning MCP server instructions in `.nax/mcp-lock.json`; the text is sanitised for control characters and capped, not locked.
Filtering MCP instructions per tool after deny or ask rules; a provider with at least one advertised tool gets its instructions delivered.
Substituting `{workdir}` in the server's own instructions; only the config text is substituted.
Recording MCP instructions in prompt-audit; the `info` attach log line is the visibility signal.
MCP instructions on nax-agent's own `createAgentSession` path (the nax-agent ACP server); only nax's sessions get them.
Removing broad `.gitignore` rules automatically; precheck and `nax init` only report them.
A loud failed-ledger signal in pipeline-mode finish (`finish/advise.ts`), which ignores git exit codes today.
A dry-run-specific branch in `commitPrdProgress`.
Committing `prd.json` from the parallel worktree executor; its unified executor stays the single writer.
E2e result parsing into per-test findings; a red e2e gate carries the output tail like every repo gate.
MCP instructions for sessions opened by `runtime/session-run-hop.ts` outside the op hop path; only `build-hop-callback-hop.ts` hops carry them.
Rewording the guard's backstop refusal: a stash command whose git invocation the guard cannot classify (`time git stash pop`) is still refused with `STASH_REFUSAL`.
Changing the workflow fix prompt's TDD wording; only the implement and fresh restart prompts change.
